architecture: rpc.rs: /ws auth (Bearer header or single-use 60s ticket, fail-closed) + loopback-only Origin gate for unauthenticated browsers; two pump tasks bridge the socket to handle_socket, a sequential JSON-RPC dispatch loop; WsClient implements ClientChannel with pending-map waiters (PendingGuard), 10s SEND_TIMEOUT, sticky stalled flag; session/prompt takes a PROMPT_SLOTS permit and registers (conn_id, CancellationToken) in live_prompts under one lock; disconnect cancels only its own conn_id entries.
report:
COVERAGE: src/rpc.rs:1-300, 301-715; re-reads at 126-237, 456-487, 562-632, 685-694 for line-exact evidence.

FINDINGS:

[F1, Medium, concurrency/performance] live_prompts Mutex held across awaited store calls blocks cancel/cleanup/prompt dispatch for ALL connections. Location: src/rpc.rs:564-596 (session/prompt) and 456-487 (session/delete task). Evidence — src/rpc.rs:564-565: `let mut map = state.live_prompts.lock().await; match state.store.session_exists(&session_id).await {`; src/rpc.rs:458-466: `let map = state.live_prompts.lock().await; if map.contains_key(&session_id) { ... match state.store.delete_session(&session_id).await {`. Scenario: with a slow DB (locked SQLite file, large message-heavy delete_session, fsync stall), session/prompt acquires the live_prompts mutex at :564 and awaits session_exists at :565 while holding it; session/delete's spawned task holds the same mutex across delete_session at :458/:466. Any other connection's session/cancel (:664), disconnect cleanup (:686), or session/prompt on any session blocks on that mutex for the whole store call. Observed misbehavior: a multi-second delete stalls cancel/prompt dispatch for every WS and relay client daemon-wide; a wedged DB turns live_prompts into a global convoy. Fix: do the store check outside the lock, then take the lock only to re-verify contains_key and insert (delete already re-checks under the lock, so a stale exists-check cannot insert into a deleted session); or have session/delete insert a tombstone while deleting that the prompt path honors.

[F2, Medium, error handling/resource semantics] `stalled` flag is sticky for the connection lifetime — one transient 10s send timeout permanently and silently drops all notifications. Location: src/rpc.rs:162-177 (notify) with :127-128, :268; no reset anywhere in the file. Evidence — src/rpc.rs:172-175: `Err(_) => { self.stalled.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed); warn!("dropping notification to stalled client"); }` (only store(true) exists; never cleared); src/rpc.rs:127-128: `/// Set once a send times out — later notifications drop immediately /// instead of each paying the full SEND_TIMEOUT again.` Scenario: a client on a slow link falls behind; the 64-slot outbound channel fills during a token-heavy turn, a single notify send exceeds SEND_TIMEOUT=10s, :173 sets stalled. notify checks stalled at :166 and returns for the rest of the process lifetime. Observed: all subsequent stream deltas/notifications on this connection are silently dropped even after the client catches up — permanently truncated assistant output, no error to client or turn; recovery requires reconnect. Fix: reset stalled to false on any successful send (or after a successful request/response exchange), or scope the flag to the active turn.

[F3, Low, boundary condition/API contract] Server-initiated request replies only matched for u64/numeric-string ids — any other id shape stalls the request until req_timeout. Location: src/rpc.rs:286-291. Evidence: `let resp_id = v["id"].as_u64().or_else(|| v["id"].as_str().and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok())); if let Some(id) = resp_id && let Some(tx) = client.pending.lock().await.remove(&id)`. Scenario: a client echoing the server's numeric id in non-canonical form — 5.0 (serde_json parses as f64), "005", " 5" — fails both parses, resp_id is None, the waiter is never resolved. Observed: the permission request (207-222) waits out the full req_timeout (permission_timeout_secs+30s, up to ~330s) before failing with 'client did not respond', though the client replied promptly; the turn then errors. Fix: fall back to an integral float match (as_f64 checked) or compare serialized forms; log the request id in WsClient::request's timeout path for diagnosability.

CLEAN (dup-exclusion material for next audit): ws_handler auth — constant-time comparison, atomic single-use ticket removal, fail-closed on unresolvable token and on missing token + non-loopback bind (30-77). is_localhost_origin — handles IPv6 brackets, trailing dots, case, ports, userinfo tricks, hex/octal IP shorthand, zone-ids, Origin:null; all fail closed; authenticated connections correctly exempt (79-91, 700-715). PROMPT_SLOTS permit freed on all paths incl. panic via catch_unwind (571-611). PendingGuard Drop + explicit removals complete on cancel/timeout/success. WS pumps terminate when peer channels drop — no leak (93-105). conn_id ownership: disconnect cancels only own entries; turn removal guarded by conn_id match — no cross-turn entry deletion (628-632, 685-691). One-prompt-per-session and insert-into-dying-session race closed via single-lock discipline (436-487, 562-596). session/cancel responds even as a request; empty-prompt and non-empty mcpServers rejected up front; string response ids coerced (287-291). 4 MiB frame caps bound parse memory.

NOTES: No cargo check/test run per assignment (audit-only static read). runtime.rs internals and api.rs ticket issuance owned by siblings — rpc side analyzed from contract. relay.rs assumed to pass equivalent mpsc channels. Negated candidates: ticket consumption atomic; all attempted Origin bypasses fail closed; conn_id matching prevents missed cancels and cross-turn deletion; permit/PendingGuard cleanup complete on cancel, panic, disconnect.
summary: Full audit of src/rpc.rs (1-715): ws_handler auth/Origin path, WsClient ClientChannel impl, PROMPT_SLOTS/PendingGuard, handle_socket routing + live_prompts lifecycle. 3 findings (2 Medium: lock-across-await on live_prompts; sticky stalled flag; 1 Low: strict response-id matching). Auth, ticket atomicity, Origin parsing, permit cleanup, conn_id-scoped cancellation verified clean.
